content:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak I’m seeing a p99 spike on the small-seq traffic lane. Baseline (before tweak): p95=85ms p99=220ms throughput=1.2k rps. After tweak: p95=120ms p99=380ms throughput=+10% (1.32k rps). Not great for our SLOs. Anyone else see this or have quick ideas?
maria: I saw the same in the dashboards. Looks correlated with increased microbatch sizes for <64-token requests — KV hit rate dropped ~14%. Probably more KV cache churn + kernel fallback.
jon: Can you paste the recent profiler trace? I want to check kernel-init and fallback counts.
alex: paste of the perf snapshot (trimmed):
```
trace: sample=3000 ops
kv_hit_rate: 78% (was 92%)
avg_batch_tokens: 210 (was 120)
kernel_switch_count: 42 (was 8)
median_latency_ms: 45 p95: 120 p99: 380
cpu/gpu memcpy spikes at tail
```
alex: Also saw frequent `cold_kernel_init` events in logs when microbatch > 128 tokens.
perf-bot: auto-detected regression: p99 up 73% on channel=small-seq-lane between 1723360000 and 1723459000. Attached flame snapshots. :warning:
jon: That kernel_switch_count is the smoking gun. Our kernel selector is picking larger-fused kernels for throughput, but for many short requests the extra init + KV deserialization + larger kernels hurt tail.
maria: Two levers: 1) cap max_batch_tokens so microbatches don't exceed the kernel warm path; 2) raise KV cache retention or prioritize prefix caching for short requests. Quick A/B could be: reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 and max_wait_ms 5 -> 3.
sam: Note tradeoff: reducing max_batch_tokens will shrink throughput headroom. We need to measure request mix; for PLG traffic hitting us now, 60% are <64 tokens so maybe worth it.
alex: Current scheduler config snippet:
```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_wait_ms: 5
  max_batch_size: 128
  policy: continuous
```
maria: Proposed quick experiments (run for 4h each on canary):
- experiment A: max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=3
- experiment B: max_batch_tokens=1024, max_wait_ms=5 (smaller batches, less batching latency)
- experiment C: keep tokens, increase KV retention + prefetch short-prefixes
jon: Also add metric slices for kernel_init_count and per-kernel p99. If kernel A has init cost X, we should avoid picking it for seq_len<Y. Suggest policy: if expected_batch_tokens < 512 -> prefer kernel_small (fast init) even if per-token slower.
alex: Agree. I'll add a heuristic: kernel_selector: prefer_low_init_for_predicted_batch_tokens_below: 512.
perf-bot: scheduled job: run ab_test A,B,C on canary (ids: ab-172345a, ab-172345b, ab-172345c). Will collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, kv_hit_rate, kernel_init_count.
maria: Also capture tail-lat histograms (bucket up to 2s) and export cold_kernel traces for tail requests.
sam: Action items:
- alex: deploy A/B jobs and wire new kernel_selector heuristic (today)
- jon: add kernel_init_count metric and per-kernel p99 (today)
- maria: prepare KV retention/prefetch config for C (tomorrow)
- perf-bot: run for 4h per variant and post summary (automated)
alex: quick note on expectations: I think A will reduce p99 by ~30-40ms but lose ~4-6% throughput; B more aggressive — better p99 but throughput hit ~8-12%. We'll choose based on SLO/TP tradeoffs.
jon: +1. Also we should check cold-start path for kernel fallback — maybe a small warm pool of kernel_small instances to avoid init on first microbatch.
maria: Good call. warm pool size of 8 per node for kernel_small could cut init tail.
alex: ok starting A now. Will post mid-run snapshot in ~2h. :rocket:
